items.summary: Amazon.com unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices on Oct 28, including a redesigned Echo Show 16 with night vision for pre-order at US$499.99 (S$641), an Echo Studio speaker with object recognition, a smart-home-capable Echo Dot priced at US$99.99, and an Echo Time bedside clock using sleep-sensing technology to wake users during lighter sleep without wearables. The moves come as Amazon faces growing competition from Apple's HomeView and HomePod mini 2, plus AI firms like OpenAI pursuing hardware ambitions (REUTERS).
items.title: Amazon Unveils Alexa Devices With Night Vision and Home Roles

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin called Elon Musk "a real genius" on Wednesday, according to a BBC translation of his remarks at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow. The comments followed discussions about satellite technology and close contact between their companies over Rassvet and Starlink satellites.
items.title: Putin Calls Musk a Real Genius After Satellite Talks

items.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest frontier model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. It ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. On external benchmarks evaluated without guardrails, it achieves a state-of-the-art 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, sets a new record of 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploitation, and reaches 71.0% on Collinear's CWE-bench for patching. It also jumps +89 elo points to #4 (1768) on WebDev Arena. DeepMind describes the rollout as deliberate, starting this week with a subset of cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program before broader availability. Pricing matches Gemini 4 Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
items.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon Cybersecurity Model

items.summary: Two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, Google announced the new frontier model Gemini 4 Carbon, which it says reaches thresholds in coding, agentic tasks and scientific analysis. It reportedly gains big in cybersecurity, is twice as likely to produce clean code versus Argon, scores up 89 points on WebDev Arena at number four, and beats GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 in most tests. Google says the model cannot be used yet; its release may be staged.
items.title: Google Announces Gemini 4 Carbon, a Frontier Model Not Yet Available

items.summary: A journalist reports that Google's AI Mode gives evasive answers when asked who won the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections, instead directing users to consult outside sources. The reporter tested this by asking directly about past elections, finding detailed responses for earlier years but indirect guidance for recent ones. Other staffers confirmed inconsistent results depending on which election was queried.
items.title: Google AI Mode Deflects Questions About Recent Elections

items.summary: Anthropic announced a suite of reporting tools that let enterprise managers view team output, cost and workflow breakdowns over any date range. The company says it will not use this data to train models by default. Anthropic's own financials show an operating profit in Q2 2025 and 900% net revenue retention. A Jellyfish report covering 276,000 customers found spending on tools like Claude Code grew 10x since the start of the year.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Reporting Tools for AI Token Spending

items.summary: Google Search's built-in AI feature, called AI Mode or the Gemini app, reportedly refuses to state that Joe Biden won the 2020 United States election. It instead directs users to a Federal Election Commission document and deflects questions about whether the vote was stolen. The tool answered confidently when asked about Donald Trump winning in 2016 and 2024. A Google spokesperson pointed Fast Company to its Bluesky response, saying it is looking into the issue. One U.S.-based colleague reportedly needed eight attempts before AI Mode acknowledged Biden's victory.
items.title: Google's AI Mode declines to confirm Biden won in U.S.

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple has announced new touchscreen MacBook Pros featuring the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, available for preorder starting at $2,899 with general availability beginning Friday, Nov. 6. The laptops include a tandem OLED display called ProLED XDR, scaling to 2,000 nits of brightness and supporting Apple's Dynamic Island feature first introduced on the iPhone. Available in both 14- and 16-inch sizes, the devices offer up to 128GB of unified memory and weigh less than previous models. ZDNET notes that while touchscreen laptops are not new, this marks a notable shift for Apple after years opposing them.
items.title: Apple Announces Touchscreen MacBook Pro With OLED Display and M5 Chips

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Discord is introducing Server Web Pages for large servers with over 1,000 members and at least eight weeks of age. From mid-December 2026, summaries of public channel conversations may appear in web searches like Google or DuckDuckGo. DMs and group chats stay private, and both admins and users can opt out through server settings.
items.title: Discord’s Discoverable Servers May Appear in Google Search Results

items.summary: Google launched its Connected Apps Platform, letting businesses submit apps that run across Google's AI features in Search and Gemini. The preview is currently available in beta to U.S. developers who sign up for the waitlist; Google did not share when it would become more broadly available. It already has over 50 connected apps in Gemini, with more coming to Search over the next few weeks.
items.title: Google Opens Gemini and Search to More Apps

items.summary: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.75% to 4% on Oct 28, in a 10-2 vote that saw Fed governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissent for a quarter-point hike. Officials cited an “accumulation of more information” before the midterms and flagged inflation as still elevated above its 2% goal. With consumer prices at 3.7%, traders expect hikes from December into 2027, while markets reacted mildly to the decision.”,
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Amid Election-Year Inflation Watch

items.summary: Meta announced PyTorch 2.15, built from 3,117 commits by 583 contributors since version 2.14. The release makes a rewritten NCCL backend the default for every nccl process group on NVIDIA hardware, paired with a flight recorder that writes a post-mortem to disk when a collective hangs and publishes watchdog health so any stalled rank triggers dumps from all ranks. It adds one-sided transports via NIXL, FSDP2 memory and communication controls including fp32 precision-sensitive parameters and CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, faster NVFP4 decode on Blackwell GPUs, FP8 support on Apple Silicon with a 1.32–1.34x MoE decode gain, FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, ROCm 10.0 wheels, Python 3.11 to 3.15 support, and CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel. Python 3.10 and macOS 14 are no longer supported. A Q&A webinar is scheduled for Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 11 AM PT with Tristan Rice, Natalia Gimelshein, Huy Do, and Jane Xu presenting. The authors encourage users to try the release and report issues as they improve it.
items.title: PyTorch Ships Version 2.15 with Rewritten NCCL Default

items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Carbon, described as its strongest model to date, built for long-horizon agentic coding and cybersecurity defense. It ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59, leading 15 of 17 published benchmarks versus Argon, GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, including 96.2% BFS F1 on GraphWalks against 84.2% for Argon. Access begins with a vetted group of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program; pricing matches Argon's introductory rate of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google noted independent replication is not yet available.
items.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber defense and coding

items.summary: Databricks frames context-grounded voice agents as a way to capture and act on customer conversations in real time, arguing that value comes only when an agent knows who is calling. It notes enterprise AI has largely faced inward toward employee assistants, while the larger opportunity sits with customers and partners daily. Citing Gartner's prediction that agentic AI will autonomously resolve 80% of common issues by 2029 for a 30% operational cost reduction, Databricks recommends starting with a 90-day pilot on one high-volume routine call. The DIVA blueprint is offered as an open-source starting point, and the article points to a demo showing real-time decisions made within roughly 200 milliseconds of human conversation pace.
items.title: Databricks Positions Context-Driven Voice Agents as New Customer Service Channel

items.summary: The article examines how prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket have grown in popularity, particularly during the 2026 election cycle. It notes that more than $220 million has been bet on the 2026 midterm elections so far. The piece raises concerns about foreign interference, insider trading, financial barriers to participation, and how these markets are sometimes misrepresented as reliable polling tools. It argues they may expand and restrict democratic participation while undermining public trust in elections.
items.title: Prediction Markets Rise Amid Concerns Over Democracy and Elections

items.summary: On Oct. 28, 2026, an article by Imane Bello argues Canada and Europe need a shared way to assess frontier AI they cannot access. It opens with the IMF steering committee's chair statement using 'advanced intelligence technologies,' while Washington pushes 'superintelligence.' The piece contends superintelligence already means something humans have not yet reached, so it loses its meaning as an alert line, and that capability thresholds shift over time—Anthropic rewrote its chemical-biological weapons threshold in May. It notes METR's tests became unreliable above 16 hrs in May, Europe's AI Act proxies for high impact via a training-compute figure of 10²⁵ operations, and signatories from 29 countries plus the European Commission backed a Finland-Norway call to convene states when thresholds are crossed. LawZero's Yoshua Bengio warns internal models used before release escape outside visibility; OpenAI released over 700 manuscripts in September and an internal model reportedly pulled hospital-bed data.
items.title: Canada and Europe Seek Shared AI Capability Thresholds

items.summary: Edmund Goh, a forum participant, describes persistent water seepage at his home over about six months that management corporation strata title (MCST) staff could not confirm after repeated visual inspections. He argues the MCST’s reliance on unqualified assessments risks incorrect diagnoses and further damage, so he proposes requiring technical assessments by qualified professionals for unresolved defects beyond a set period, clear escalation guidelines for managing agents, and enforcement mechanisms when they fail to comply.
items.title: Proposed enforcement for unresolved estate defects in Singapore

items.summary: Tapas Ganguly reported that approximately 3,600 recent university graduates were still seeking employment in June despite available entry-level vacancies. He questioned whether jobs are effectively matched with qualified young Singaporeans and called for the Ministry of Manpower to establish a proactive system identifying unemployed graduates. He urged agencies to engage these individuals directly and noted concerns about advertised positions receiving no responses.
items.title: Graduate Employment Matching Concern Raised in Forum Post

items.summary: Will Knight deployed AI agents, built with OpenAI's Codex, to manage an experimental Premier League fantasy roster. The initial suggestions were poor—leaving Erling Haaland on the bench—but adding specialized agents improved them; scaling past 100 agents changed little besides raising his API bill. His team has not outscored the average recently, so he will use none of its picks. Knight notes AI predictions are improving fast: computer scientist Haifeng Xu says models now consume large amounts of real-world information and orchestrate complex systems. In testing, GPT-5 ranked best at predicting outcomes like the NBA Championship winner.
items.title: AI Agents Manage a Fantasy Soccer Team

items.summary: The article argues that modern engineering increasingly blends human judgment with machine capability, and that systems thinking is essential as projects span multiple specialties. It describes how an engineer can use AI to search research, generate design options, run simulations, and compare results before bringing findings to specialists for checks on safety, context, ethics, and usability—leaving the final decision a human responsibility. The piece notes AI cannot replace deep expertise or judgment in areas involving values and accountability, so engineers must decide where each belongs. It frames engineering as an adaptable way of thinking rather than mastery of every field, then points to IEEE’s role in building communities around cross-disciplinary problems like trustworthy clinical AI and safe autonomous systems, and in setting standards for human-machine collaboration.
items.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI

items.summary: Ford has produced more than 5,000 large aluminum unicastings for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch. Each truck uses two castings, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts in a method modeled on Tesla's Giga Press approach popularized six years ago. The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford's chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, via the From the Road blog; the work happens at Shelbyville Technical Center before shipping to Louisville Assembly Plant for testing. Critics note that while fewer parts look promising, repair cost remains a concern and Ford is catching up rather than leapfrogging Tesla.
items.title: Ford Casts Over 5,000 Unicastings for Its Fathom EV Truck

items.summary: The Department of Energy announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion on Tuesday to boost the output of 15 reactors at eight nuclear power plants in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania by a combined 1.1 gigawatts. The move expands clean power capacity faster than building new reactors. It is the third multibillion-dollar uprate announcement for Constellation Energy within a month, following deals with Amazon and Google. Constellation stressed that the commitment does not represent a final decision to proceed at every facility. Analysts note it could be a cost-effective alternative to constructing AP1000 reactors, though funding may support separate projects from those backed by hyperscalers. Constellation did not respond to requests for clarification. Erik Cothron of the Nuclear Innovation Alliance called the loan evidence that uprates are cost-effective with reasonable repayment prospects.
items.title: DOE Approves $5 Billion Loan for Constellation Nuclear Uprates

items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee approved a statement by a 10 – 2 vote on October 28, 2026, keeping the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The Committee cited strong economic activity and resilient spending while noting that inflation remains elevated above its 2 percent goal. Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack voted against the action, preferring a quarter-point increase.
items.title: Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates at 3-3/4 to 4 Percent

items.summary: At its investor day in Las Vegas, Oracle CFO Hilary Maxson said the company expects capital spending to peak this fiscal year and next as it builds cloud capacity. She pledged no more than $20 billion in additional financing through fiscal 2030, split evenly between debt and equity, to reassure investors about its AI buildout funding needs.
items.title: Oracle Cites Financing Cap to Ease AI Spending Concerns

items.summary: Alphabet's Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model focused on cybersecurity tasks such as vulnerability discovery, exploitation and software patching. Launched two weeks after the coding-oriented Gemini 4 Argon, it is aimed at developers and enterprise customers. The company said Carbon generates secure code at more than twice the success rate of Gemini 4 Argon on internal benchmarks. It will be offered first through Google's Fairwind Program while testing safeguards, priced to match Gemini 4 Argon's introductory rates.
items.title: Google Unveils Cybersecurity-Focused Gemini 4 Carbon AI Model

items.summary: Investors and journalists examined Anthropic's IPO filing, which reported an $80 billion net loss but highlighted an 85% gross profit margin on running its existing AI models. As The Information described it, the figure is 'a reality check' for skeptics doubting profitability of pay-as-you-go pricing. Analysts note the margin excludes training costs and compares favorably to Meta's ad machine at roughly 81-82%. Anthropic remains unprofitable overall.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Reveals High Gross Margin

items.summary: Apple introduced its high-end MacBook Pro with a tandem PROLED XDR display and touchscreen support, the company said. The laptop adds a glowing Apple logo on the rear as another design element. It comes in two familiar sizes: 14 inches and 16 inches, but with bigger upgrades on the display front.
items.title: Apple Unveils OLED MacBook Pro With Touchscreen Display

items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%, with two officials dissenting for a quarter-point hike, the first split since September. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack cast the opposing votes amid political pressure from Donald Trump over Cook's conduct. The post-meeting statement flagged elevated inflation while noting strong growth, arriving just before the November midterm elections.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady in Split Vote Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Markets focus on a Federal Reserve decision, with roughly a 90% chance rates hold steady after the September 0.25 percentage point lift. Investors watch for signals from Chairman Kevin Warsh as benchmark Treasury yields climb above 5%. AI-linked stocks face pressure over funding concerns, though strategist Mike Wilson says most of the correction may be over. Overseas markets mixed, with South Korea's Kospi up and Europe slightly lower.
items.title: Wall Street Awaits Fed and Tech Earnings

items.summary: Deductors and tax collectors must meet several tax deductions at source (TDS) and tax collection at source (TCS) deadlines in October and November 2026, covering quarterly statements for the July-September quarter plus tax deposits and challan-cum-statements. These fall within the first full year under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which revised several form numbers. Experts advised deductors to familiarise themselves with the updated forms and file on time to avoid penalties.
items.title: India's TDS and TCS Compliance Deadlines in October and November 2026

items.summary: The Guardian’s economics editor Heather Stewart and political editor Pippa Crerar examine the chancellor’s budget, covering what he announced, his reasoning behind it, and notable omissions. The briefing frames these as the central questions to be answered.
items.title: Guardian editors assess chancellor's budget key questions

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey directed every government department to find a 1% cut in their capital budgets, aiming to fill a £4.7bn shortfall in the funding of the Defence Investment Plan. The reductions add to earlier cuts made this year toward the plan's overall £15bn price tag. Under pressure over how he will reach spending 3% of national income on defence by 2030, Healey said details would be set out at next year's spending review and mentioned innovative financing with allies. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch dismissed it as 'a plan to have a plan.' Government departments still need to decide what to cut from their capital budgets.
items.title: Healey Orders Departments for 1% Capital Cuts to Fund Defence

items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged at Wednesday's meeting, though it signaled continued resistance to inflation. The central bank renewed its price-stability pledge amid energy-price spikes linked to the U.S.-Iran war and a 3.7% year-over-year rise in consumer prices. Economists note AI investment and resilient spending may offset tightening, while lower-income households face declining purchasing power as wages rose just 3%. A December rate hike is now widely expected.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady Amid Stubborn Inflation

items.summary: An audit of research by Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman found errors across 138 papers, with 2,035 problems identified. Of these, 147 were serious enough to change a headline number, and 69% of the audited papers had at least one problem. Among major and moderate errors, 97% have a clear direction that overstates each paper's claim. The work was produced through two independent audits per paper plus adjudication by a third agent.
items.title: AI Audit Finds Widespread Errors in Saez and Zucman Research

items.summary: Tianyu Jiang, a University of Michigan job-market candidate co-authoring with Yuqing (Claire) Wang, studies how generative AI reshapes research productivity in economics. Using NBER records, LLM-assisted writing measures, and a survey of 227 economists, the study finds productivity gaps among authors narrowed after ChatGPT's release but that greater AI exposure widens output gaps between senior and junior researchers.
items.title: AI's uneven impact on economics research productivity

items.summary: A blog author, who has long expressed skepticism toward President Trump’s tariffs announced in April 2025, recommends a six-paper symposium on tariffs published in the Summer 2026 issue of the Journal of Economic Perspectives. The papers cover historical tariff data back to 1789, labor market disruptions from trade liberalization, Pigouvian perspectives on taxing trade, whether foreign producers or US consumers bear tariff costs, and macroeconomic versus industrial policy responses. Gita Gopinath and Brent Neiman estimate that through the end of 2025, actual rates were about half of statutory ones, with more than 90% passed through to US buyers. Another paper estimates tariffs at 2025 levels would raise $2.5 trillion over 10 years. The author notes Trump imposed them without Congress and claims they will enrich the country.
items.title: All About Tariffs

items.summary: Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk’s genius while speaking at a summit with African leaders in Moscow, saying he was in close contact with Starlink’s controlling shareholder. Comparing SpaceX’s Earth-orbiting network to Russia’s Rassvet constellation, the Russian leader said Musk had more than 5,000 satellites in orbit and that Russia is only taking its first steps; the true number of active SpaceX satellites is estimated at about 10,000. Moscow has begun developing an alternative system with an estimated 26 working satellites, though its capacity remains limited. Putin said contact with American partners helps avoid interference in orbit as Russia develops satellite communications for military use against Ukraine.
items.title: Putin Praises Musk as Russia Builds Own Satellite Network

items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its interest rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, matching the more than 90% of analysts who expected no change and arriving less than a week before midterm elections amid an affordability crisis driven by inflation. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh had earlier surprised President Donald Trump with a September rate hike.
items.title: The Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Google announced its new frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, on Wednesday, calling it the company's strongest with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. The firm claimed first place on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59, plus an 89-point jump to fourth on the WebDev Arena leaderboard. It will launch for cybersecurity defenders this week before broader rollout, with introductory pricing set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google also said internal testing showed Carbon cuts unsupported claims by about half versus Argon while stating methodological caveats directly rather than fabricating missing evidence.
items.title: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon AI Model

items.summary: In Arizona's affluent, fiercely contested first congressional district, the question of whether Donald Trump helps or hurts its candidates divides voters. Lifelong Republican Tom Wolfe called Trump's endorsement a 'death knell,' while retired accountant David McGahan said he likes the country's course under Trump. The open seat follows congressman David Schweikert declining to run again. Republicans' hold has slipped since 2016, though they keep a registration edge. Nikki Haley won nearly 25% of the district vote in the 2024 primary even after Trump clinched the nomination; Trump's margin there was 3%, versus 5.5% statewide. Cook Political Report now rates the Feely-Shah race as leaning Democrat, though Feely backers argue it remains conservative at heart and independents will decide on 3 November.
items.title: Arizona's Wealthiest District Weighs Trump in Midterm Race

items.summary: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has arrived in the US amid ongoing uncertainty about his whereabouts, according to BBC Verify. The US state department told the BBC on Tuesday it will issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family. BBC Verify reconstructed his journey through Brazil, Argentina and Ecuador before reaching Miami.
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro's Path From Brazil To Miami

items.summary: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured over 100 on Wednesday, authorities said, with the toll likely to rise. Officials call it one of Europe's deadliest such disasters this century. The second accident to strike Spain this year raises questions about rail safety; transport minister Sarah Morris spoke of an 'error' and 'inexplicable circumstances.'
items.title: Spain High-Speed Train Crash Kills 68

items.summary: An effort led by the Freshwater Research Centre and Cape Nature has removed invasive spotted bass from about 8 km [5 mi] of the upper Breekkrans River, extending the habitat of the critically endangered doring fiery redfin from 2 km to 10 km. Jeremy Shelton said mechanical methods eradicated the fish permanently. Martine Jordaan noted all native species recovered as their range increased since 2023.
items.title: Bass Eradication Expands Range of Endangered South African Fish

items.summary: Geopolitical analyst Barry Healy, a protester against Australia's AUKUS nuclear submarine programme, visited China for the first time and reflected on how it reshaped his views. On The PointCast he described being moved by the sacrifices of the Long March and struck by the transformation of once-impoverished villages, gaining a new perspective on China's history and development.
items.title: Australian Analyst Rethinks China After First Visit

items.summary: This page introduces a program about the Long March, described as an odyssey unequaled in modern times. Panelists Rafael Zerbetto, Barry Healy, Wang Xinsong, and Sidne Ward explore its history, decisions, and lessons for young people today.
items.title: Experts Reflect on Lessons From China's Long March Odyssey

items.summary: Kyar Moe Tun, Myanmar's UN ambassador appointed before the military ousted the elected government in 2021, broke down during a speech urging member states to stop their silence and help end the crisis. He said the international community had failed the people of Myanmar again and again.
items.title: Myanmar UN Ambassador Breaks Down Urging World to End Suffering

items.summary: Youth justice and child safety unionised staff in Queensland's south-east corner will walk off the job today, marking their longest stop action since 2018. Together Union delegates say highly experienced caseworkers are leaving amid crushing workloads and fewer resources. Mount Isa delegate Karlie Markham said the Youth Justice Service Centre lost a collective 50 years of experience in the last 12 months. A Crisafulli government spokesperson said contingency plans were in place to minimise disruption.
items.title: Queensland youth justice and child safety workers stage longest stop action since 2018

items.summary: Indi MP Helen Haines's offices are reopening little more than a week after she was attacked, which left her requiring a double amputation. Her team says the offices will be open three days a week for the rest of the year and thanked the community for its support. Ms Haines has been granted a leave of absence, while Leader of the House Tony Burke told parliament resolutions would be moved for as long as they were needed.
items.title: Helen Haines's offices reopen after attack that led to amputation

items.summary: Harvesting has stopped in parts of Michoacán, Mexico’s leading avocado producer and exporter, after small growers called a strike demanding up to 45 pesos ($2.40) per kilogram versus the roughly 13 pesos ($0.70) they currently receive. The Union of Small Producers of Michoacán (PUAM), led by Valentín Rodríguez, set roadblocks at plant health boards required for exports and said only about 600 of 1,100 containers scheduled this week are now expected to ship after two days without harvesting. The U.S., which accounts for 99% of growers’ market, buys $3.65 billion worth annually. APEAM says it is open to proposals; Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla urged diversifying markets beyond the United States.
items.title: Avocado Growers’ Strike Halts Mexico’s U.S. Exports

items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, six days before the US midterms. The committee split 10-2, with Governors Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voting for another quarter-point hike; Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan backed holding. Inflation stood at 3.7%, though markets still expect a December rise. The statement noted inflation remains elevated while activity was expanding at a strong pace. Speaking after the vote, Chair Kevin Warsh said domestic spending has been resilient but inflation remains elevated and more information would help decide policy stance.
items.title: Fed Holds Rates as Cook and Hammack Push for Hike

items.summary: In Brazil’s 2026 presidential election, the first round on Oct. 4 was driven by resentment among those displaced by automation and new self-employment, favoring far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro over President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. But in the runoff on Oct. 25, motivation shifted to fear of a return of “Bolsonarismo.” Lula’s street campaign, social media mobilization through WhatsApp network “Lula’s Army,” and surprise results reversed his lackluster first-round showing. Fear intensified as Flávio Bolsonaro drew comparisons to jailed father Jair Bolsonaro. Voter alienation fell: 4.8 million electors returned, invalid votes dropped from 3.7 million to 2.7 million, blank ballots from 2.3 million to 1.4 million. The article notes this may narrow Lula’s congressional room for maneuver starting in 2027 as center-right and right forces gain weight.
items.title: Brazilian Voters Shift from Resentment to Fear in Lula’s Reelection

items.summary: UEFA moved a Europa League match between Rennes and Olympiacos forward by one day, setting kick-off for 4.30pm on Wednesday 4 November instead of Thursday 5 November. The change follows a general strike called by French unions that same day. UEFA said the French authorities warned it could not guarantee usual security arrangements in Rennes then. Some Rennes supporters have criticised the timing.
items.title: UEFA Moves Rennes Clash Ahead of French Strike

items.summary: A ceasefire took effect in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region on October 27. Former residents who escaped told DW they faced hunger, no medicine and no electricity or water, while about 2,000 people remain trapped. According to the Save Ukraine Foundation, it has rescued at least 300 civilians over the past six months. Lawyer Myroslava Kharchenko, who works for the organization, said mine-clearing on roads began around 8 a.m., but details inside Oleshky stay confidential. The foundation estimates around 500 people may eventually be evacuated, likely through temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory and possibly Russia.
items.title: Preparations Underway for Oleshky Evacuation After Ceasefire

items.summary: Apple announced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, featuring an OLED display and touch controls for the premium lineup. The new 14-inch model starts at $2,899 in the US; the 16-inch model is priced at $3,399. These prices are about $400 higher than previous M5 Pro models after June price increases, driven by OLED technology and redesigned hardware. Models will debut at Apple's “Pro and Tell” event on October 28.
items.title: Apple Unveils Touchscreen MacBook Pro With OLED Displays

items.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus unveiled the company's first touchscreen MacBooks on Wednesday, ending years of resistance to touchscreens in laptops. The launch capped a series of product reveals ahead of holiday shopping. Analyst Anshel Sag called it inevitable. Reports suggest the new models use existing M5 Pro and Max chips without major performance gains.
items.title: Apple's John Ternus Unveils First Touchscreen MacBooks at Product Event

items.summary: Dr Mihirkant Upadhyaya, a senior supply chain technical programme manager at Intel in Hillsboro, Oregon, is expected to graduate from the University of Washington's Foster School of Business with an MBA in Supply Chain and Operations in June 2027. He holds five prior qualifications, including a PhD in Nanoscale Science and Engineering completed in 2014. His current role spans supplier relationships, equipment procurement and compliance across international markets. The article notes the programme could complement his technical background with business strategy knowledge, but states these are potential benefits rather than a confirmed explanation of his decision, since his profile does not specify his motivation or career targets. He also completed an Everest Base Camp trek in spring 2025 at 5,364 metres and plans a summit attempt in 2028.
items.title: Intel Engineer Pursues MBA While Climbing Everest

items.summary: The US Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged at 3.75%-4% in a 10-2 vote ahead of the midterm elections. Chair Kevin Warsh upgraded economic activity to “strong” and said inflation expectations had improved since September. Governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, favouring a 25-basis-point hike amid persistent inflation above the 2% target. Markets reacted cautiously as further increases remain possible if prices do not ease.
items.title: Federal Reserve Holds Rates, Keeps Hikes Possible

items.summary: Samsung unveiled its first cuff-style earbuds, the $229 Galaxy Buds On, on Wednesday (date-705-713). The C-shaped clip-on design hugs the earlobe while leaving the ear canal open for ambient awareness. Samsung said it developed them through an AI-driven computational process using over 119 million ear-data points (quantity-890-910). Battery life is rated at 9.5 hours of continuous playback — the longest of any Galaxy Bud product to date, per the company (quantity-1601-1610) — reaching up to 38 hours with case top-offs (quantity-1912-1920).
items.title: Samsung Unveils Galaxy Buds On Clip-On Earbuds

items.summary:
Indian cyber security experts say Instagram and YouTube reels have become free surveillance for criminals planning attacks on film stars, citing Mumbai Crime Branch notes that the men sent to kill Sanjay Dutt had never visited Mumbai before September 20. Experts describe how location tags, visible number plates and fan-page repetition let networks build movement maps of celebrities' routines, with liability remaining scattered until platform obligations begin in May 2027.

items.summary: The US goods trade deficit widened more than expected in September, reaching $134.9 billion per the Commerce Department's Census Bureau, its highest level since March 2025. The surge was driven by capital goods imports climbing to a record $344.1 billion, with capital goods alone up 77.2% year-on-year as tech firms source AI hardware overseas. Economists surveyed by Reuters estimated the deficit would reach $130.2 billion and warned it could drag third-quarter GDP growth by four percentage points, though Oxford Economics put the figure at 3.25%. Nationwide's Daniel Vielhaber called trade a sign of strength amid continued business investment, while Santander US Capital Markets' Stephen Stanley attributed the gap to overseas hardware demand.
items.title: US Goods Trade Deficit Widens as AI Boom Fuels Record Imports

items.summary: Vedanta Aluminium reported Q2 revenue of Rs 22,066 crore, up 41% year-on-year. Net profit fell 6% to Rs 6,597 crore sequentially as an exceptional charge of Rs 363 crore weighed in. Quarterly aluminium production hit a record 649,000 tonnes, while EBITDA rose 83%. CEO Rajesh Kumar cited momentum in scaling the integrated business.
items.title: Vedanta Aluminium Posts Record Production Amid Profit Dip

items.summary: Captain Smit Machchhar of flydubai received the First Class Order of Zayed II from UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan at a Dubai reception, with medals presented by Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan. A visible line of stitches across his head highlighted injuries sustained when his co-pilot allegedly attacked him inside the cockpit during flight FZ1073 on September 30 en route to Tel Aviv.
items.title: UAE Honours Indian Pilot for Thwarting Cockpit Attack

items.summary: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) extended its support to the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan against alleged electoral irregularities. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the voter revision raised concerns about excluding eligible voters and accused the Election Commission of undermining democracy, stating that people choose government, not vice versa. The opposition is intensifying its campaign ahead of the rally.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party backs INDIA bloc rally
